narrative.overview:
Neoflow is a ledger you read in a terminal: rows of code, Messages and Responses, each set down plainly and kept. The screen is mostly text on a low, slightly tinted ground, dark or light to match the terminal. Panes are outlined with thin rounded rules and filled with a surface one step off the ground. Nothing glows, slides in or decorates. When the eye catches on something, it is because that thing is focused, selected or changed state.

Density is deliberate. A developer runs Neoflow in a split pane beside a harness and an editor, so every row earns its place and secondary facts step back by dimming, not by shrinking or hiding. Hierarchy comes from weight (bold titles), position (the focused pane's `▌` marker) and a small set of tinted washes behind selected and changed rows.

Every visual signal has a plain-text equivalent. A state is always a glyph and a word, and color adds a third channel on top. That is why `--no-color` and `--ascii` work as full modes rather than degraded fallbacks.
keyCharacteristics: Tinted ground with a one-step-offset pane surface; light and dark presets share one role set, and the default follows the terminal.
Thin rounded pane borders (`╭╮╰╯`) that switch to `+ - |` under `--ascii`.
One accent per theme. It marks focus and selection, nothing else.
Every state is a glyph, a word and a color tone. Color is never the only channel.
Bold titles, muted metadata, no size hierarchy (the terminal has one size).
Motion only where it carries meaning: a braille spinner for work in progress and optional eased scrolling.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Each theme has a single accent, and it means focus or selection. It never decorates, never marks success and never marks a warning.

rules.name: The Washes Are Rows Rule
rules.body: Tinted washes (`*-wash`) fill whole rows behind content. They never sit behind isolated words or labels.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Text clears 4.5:1 on every fill in its theme, washes included, and a new theme or role is checked against that matrix before it ships. Quiet Paper meets it fully. The dark presets' Pewter and comment text fall to 3.8–4.4:1 on row washes, which is a known gap to close, not a precedent.

rules.name: The Transparent Terminal Rule
rules.body: With `background: terminal`, every fill (ground, pane, raised, washes) becomes transparent and only foreground colors remain. Under `--no-color`, every role collapses to plain white on transparent.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Promote with bold and demote with Pewter. Uppercase is reserved for short mode or state labels, never for sentences.

rules.name: The Code Keeps the Room Rule
rules.body: When space runs out, chrome collapses first (header to one row, then one pane at a time). The Diff never shrinks to make room for chrome.

rules.name: The Three Steps Rule
rules.body: Only Ground, Pane and Raised exist. A fourth surface level means the design needs restructuring, not another tint.

dos: **Do** express every state as glyph, word and tone through `reviewingStatus.ts`, so it reads the same in all three places it appears.
**Do** keep the reader's place: a refresh, an answer landing or a list toggle keeps the selected file and Diff line (matched by path and line).
**Do** ask for a second Esc before throwing away typed text; an empty draft closes on one.
**Do** give every Unicode glyph an ASCII twin and every color a meaning that survives `--no-color`.
**Do** add new colors as roles in `SemanticTheme` with values in all three themes, never as one-off hex literals in views.
**Do** collapse chrome before code at narrow widths (one-row header, then single pane below 90 columns).
**Do** show the visible window as ordinals (`· 12-40/310`) rather than drawing scrollbars.
**Do** fit text to the width it actually has. Wrap instructions and recovery sentences; never let OpenTUI's middle truncation cut them.
donts: **Don't** use the accent for anything except focus and selection.
**Don't** put a wash behind a single word, or add a fourth surface tint.
**Don't** animate anything except the work-in-progress spinner and opt-in eased scrolling (`motion: off` disables the latter).
**Don't** rely on color alone to separate states. If two states differ only by color, give them different glyphs.
**Don't** pair a dark-only preset (Warm Carbon, Indigo Night) with a light terminal and expect legibility. Only Match terminal and Quiet Paper are built for light backgrounds.
**Don't** let a theme's warning share its accent's hue. Caution and focus must stay distinguishable.
